newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees Q1 fall in revenues vs Q4.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees Q1 fall in revenues vs Q4.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Friday it expects revenues to fall in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the fourth quarter of 1996.

In fourth quarter results released late Thursday, the company surprised analysts with an increase of sales to $7.7 billion versus $7.3 billion last year. Analysts had expected sales in the range of $7.0 billion for the fourth quarter.
"A decline in revenues from the fourth quarter of 1996 to the first quarter of 1997 is expected," Ed Gams, head of investor relations, told analysts in a conference call.
Gams reiterated the company does not expect a return to overall increased profitability until later in 1997, citing overcapacity and competitive pricing in the semiconductor business.
Motorola sees growth of eight to 10 percent industry-wide in semiconductors in 1997, but said it expects that recovery to be gradual and therefore Motorola's rebound to be gradual as well.
"Our projection for worldwide semiconductor industry growth for 1997 is eight to 10 percent, with the strongest growth in the Asia Pacific and the Americas," Gams said.
"We continue to believe the recovery from the semiconductor industry recessionary cycle of 1996 has begun; however, we also continue to believe that the recovery will be gradual," Gams said.
Motorola reported fourth quarter semiconductor sales were down 18 percent and orders fell 11 percent from 1995, but compared with third quarter, orders rose more than 20 percent.
Although Motorola said it expects all end-markets which use semiconductors to grow in 1997, over capacity will keep the recovery modest and prevent average selling prices from increasing.
"This will continue to place significant pressure on our semiconductor profitability, particularly for the first quarter of 1997 versus the first quarter of 1996," Gams said.
